summary: Evidence packet for the runx postmortem-maker skill (automerchlab/postmortem-maker@1.0.0). The skill folds incident fragments (timeline, alerts, deploys, chat notes, policy) into a traceable postmortem without promoting unknowns to facts: every timeline row and root-cause claim cites its input evidence, hedged chat speculation stays a hypothesis, conflicting or insufficient evidence yields unknowns and NO publish proposal, and the publish_proposal that is emitted is gated (requires_approval) and consumed by a downstream send-as/doc-publisher executor — the skill posts nothing. A real post-publish dogfood run of the PUBLISHED registry package (registry_source=remote, version=1.0.0) produced a sealed runx.receipt.v1 that passes runx verify with a production signature: root_cause confirmed (webhook-dispatcher@v1.9.3 deploy 11 min before the first alert, corroborated by a declarative oncall note), impact known (312 merchant endpoints, 22 minutes), 0 unknowns, 2 action items each naming a target lane, and a gated publish proposal. source_url, X.yaml, SKILL.md and verification.json all resolve at a single source revision (commit b0ad3f4545a528a083317b92524eabf7fbdf9830); this evidence packet and the report are its direct child (same revision). The committed skill files are the files that were published as automerchlab/postmortem-maker@1.0.0 and the dogfood ran that published package, not a local path.
